verdicts.title: Geometric complexity theory and matrix powering
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Valiant's famous determinant versus permanent problem is the flagship problem in algebraic complexity theory. Mulmuley and Sohoni (Siam J Comput 2001, 2008) introduced geometric complexity theory, an approach to study this and related problems via algebraic geometry and representation theory. Their approach works by multiplying the permanent polynomial with a high power of a linear form (a process called padding) and then comparing the orbit closures of the determinant and the padded permanent.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns geometric complexity theory, orbit closures, and lower bounds for the permanent vs. matrix powering — it never addresses communication complexity, variance over inputs of length n, or NP languages as framed in the conjecture.

verdicts.title: Representation Theory of Finite Groups
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: The point of view of these notes on the topic is to bring out the flavour that Representation Theory is an extension of the first course on Group Theory. We also emphasize the importance of the base field. These notes cover completely the theory over complex numbers which is Character Theory. A large number of worked-out examples are the main feature of these notes. The prerequisite for this note is basic group theory and linear algebra.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract describes introductory notes on representation theory of finite groups over complex numbers (character theory), with no mention of communication complexity, NP languages, or variance bounds. It shares only the general vocabulary of 'representation' but does not address the specific claim.
